panels.title: Running
panels.description: Zero here is EARNED, not defaulted: the `or sum(aws_inventory_scrape_success == 1) * 0` tail yields 0 only when the sweep completed cleanly and found nothing, and leaves the panel empty when the sweep failed.

panels.title: Stopped
panels.description: Zero here is EARNED, not defaulted: the `or sum(aws_inventory_scrape_success == 1) * 0` tail yields 0 only when the sweep completed cleanly and found nothing, and leaves the panel empty when the sweep failed.

panels.title: Orphaned
panels.description: Crossplane-tagged AWS resources with NO live managed resource, confirmed fresh by Resource Explorer. Expected 0. Reads 'NO DATA' — never 0 — when the exporter could not read the live managed-resource set, because aws_orphaned_resource_count is omitted entirely in that state rather than defaulted to zero.

panels.title: Fleets
panels.description: EC2 Fleets in any non-`deleted` state. deleted_running and deleted_terminating are counted: they still own instances, so they still bill.

panels.title: Fleets not placing
panels.description: Fleets whose target capacity is above 0 while fulfilled capacity is 0: burning nothing but silently failing to place. Usually no spot capacity in the pool or a regional vCPU quota the shape cannot fit under. '—' means no fleet is in that state; read it next to the Fleets count.

panels.title: EC2 Fleets — state, activity, management
panels.description: activity_status `error` or `pending_fulfillment` on an active maintain fleet is the silent-failure signature. management=orphaned here is the worst case: a maintain fleet with no managed resource re-launches GPU capacity indefinitely and no reaper stops it.

panels.title: Drift — what AWS has that git does not
Managed
panels.description: Crossplane tags present AND a live managed resource of that kind/name exists. The join key is exact: crossplane-name IS the MR's metadata.name.

panels.title: Orphaned (fresh)
panels.description: Crossplane created it and lost it, and Resource Explorer re-confirmed it exists within the last ORPHAN_FRESH_MAX_AGE. Bills forever; nothing tracks it. Should always be 0.

panels.title: Orphan suspects
panels.description: Orphan-shaped, but seen only through a source that cannot confirm the resource still exists: the tagging API (no timestamp at all) or a stale Resource Explorer entry. Mostly index lag — us-east-2's tagging API still returns a crossplane-tagged instance that describe-instances says is gone. Confirm with the owning service before deleting anything.

panels.title: Unmanaged (review)
panels.description: No crossplane-* tags at all: console, CLI, packer or legacy. Exact without Kubernetes, because it depends only on the resource's own tags.

panels.title: Allowlisted
panels.description: Unmanaged and expected to be: default-VPC furniture, service-linked roles, per-service singletons AWS creates on first use. Counted, not alarmed.

panels.title: Inventory total
panels.description: Distinct ARNs in the merged Resource Explorer + tagging API inventory.

panels.title: MR index readable
panels.description: NO means the Kubernetes half of the join failed, so managed-vs-orphaned is undecidable and every crossplane-tagged resource sits in the `crossplane-tagged` bucket. Check rbac.yaml is armed.

panels.title: Classification trusted
panels.description: NO means every count on this dashboard is a lower bound: the MR index was incomplete, a region's scan failed, or Resource Explorer truncated a result set.

panels.title: ORPHANED — Crossplane made it, Crossplane lost it, AWS still bills

defaults.noValue: No orphans, or no scan — check 'MR index readable' before reading this as clean.

panels.description: freshness=fresh is actionable. stale/unverified need confirmation with the owning service's describe call first.

panels.title: Unmanaged & NOT allowlisted — console / CLI / packer / legacy
Inventory by service / type / region / bucket
Scan integrity & coverage — read this before believing any count
RE indexes
panels.description: Resource Explorer LOCAL/AGGREGATOR indexes that exist.

panels.title: Aggregator index
panels.description: NO means no single Search can cover the account: every index is LOCAL and answers only for its own region. Promoting one region to AGGREGATOR is an AWS write a human must run — see infrastructure/base/aws/inventory-ro-user.yaml.

panels.title: MR kinds discovered
panels.description: Managed-resource kinds found by walking the API server's discovery doc for Crossplane's `managed` category. Never a hardcoded list — a hardcoded list silently stops covering new kinds, which is the drift this exporter exists to catch.

panels.title: MR kinds listable
panels.description: Fewer than discovered means RBAC is missing an API group and the live MR set is incomplete — every managed resource of those kinds would read as an orphan.

panels.title: Coverage complete
panels.description: Trustworthy AND every enabled region scanned by some source AND an AGGREGATOR index exists. 0 = known blind spots, listed to the right.

panels.title: Zero is believable
panels.description: The single stat that says whether a 0 on the Orphaned panel means anything. YES requires the live managed-resource set read in full AND every enabled region swept cleanly with no truncation. NO means the orphan count is withheld entirely rather than defaulted — an orphan could be sitting in whatever failed.

panels.title: Scan failures — the `code` label separates AccessDenied from an empty account
panels.description: code=AccessDeniedException / UnauthorizedException means the IAM policy in infrastructure/base/aws/inventory-ro-user.yaml is missing an action. code=HTTP403 with source=kubernetes means rbac.yaml is not armed.

panels.title: Regions with NO Resource Explorer index
panels.description: Blind spots for the primary source. The tagging API covers them, but only for resources that are tagged — an untagged leak in these regions is invisible. Fix with `aws resource-explorer-2 create-index --region <r>`.

panels.title: Source divergence — Resource Explorer vs tagging API
panels.description: Per-region counts from each source. Resource Explorer should return MORE than the tagging API, because it also indexes untaggable resources.

panels.title: Seconds since last fire (drops = a reaper fired; flat climb = STOPPED firing)
